scope: MC-15 internal bilingual IA/SEO planning
evidenceNotes: No phase is executed in MC-15. Phases 1-6 describe work that future milestones and human owners may perform only after the written authorisations named per phase.
MC-16 is not started. This dataset is a planning record, not a schedule commitment, and no date is promised.

Phase 0 observations gathered during MC-15 (isolated local SSR probes documented in D07/D08/D09) are partial evidence inputs; they are not the formal Phase 0 snapshot, which requires an immutable artefact.
No Search Console access exists in MC-15, so no phase may claim indexation evidence.

items.name: Baseline preservation
items.objective: Freeze the current public URL surface as the immutable reference every later phase must preserve: route and URL inventory, canonical and hreflang map, redirect map, sitemap output, robots.txt content, HTTP status per URL and the structured-data inventory. Read-only capture; nothing may be published, moved or redirected.
scope: Read-only crawl of the local or staging SSR surface with a disposable database and the inherited test fixtures.
Record, per URL: status code, canonical, hreflang set, robots meta, X-Robots-Tag, sitemap membership, JSON-LD types, redirect location where applicable.
Record the full sitemap URL set and the robots.txt content verbatim.
Record the inherited redirect set: /open-marine -> /tecnologia, /productos -> /tecnologia, /productos/:slug -> /tecnologia/:slug (EXISTING_ACTIVE).
outOfScope: Any write to src/, public/, package.json, the sitemap generator or robots.txt.
Any deployment, release, DNS, CDN, hosting or Search Console action.
Any redirect creation, removal or re-pointing.
entryCriteria: Working tree at the frozen MC-15 base commit e0be1e457456a401a529e1912770e07ed9a863e4 with no pending writer.
MC-15 D02/D03 URL and route inventories accepted, and D07-D10 decisions available as the expected-state reference.
Read-only access to a reproducible SSR run with a disposable DATA_DIR and seeded fixtures identical to the inherited SEO gate.
exitCriteria: An immutable snapshot artefact exists containing the complete public URL set with status, canonical, hreflang, robots and sitemap membership.
The snapshot explains every difference from the registered inventories; unexplained differences block the phase.
The snapshot is referenced by name from Phase 4 and from D16, and cannot be edited after capture (append-only correction record instead).
deliverables: Pre-release URL snapshot artefact (see D16 section 2)
Snapshot verification note against the registered inventories
prohibitedActions: Publishing, deploying, redirecting, re-indexing or submitting a sitemap.
Treating the partial local probes gathered in MC-15 as the formal snapshot.
evidenceRequired: Immutable snapshot artefact with capture timestamp and source commit
Diff report between the snapshot and the registered inventories
Local SSR run log with the fixture description

items.name: Approved corporate IA planning candidates
items.objective: Turn the corporate information architecture into a reviewed candidate list that can be implemented later: which page identities exist, which entity each one represents, which locale paths are proposed, what the collision and canonical/hreflang consequence is, and that none of them is pre-authorised for publication or indexation.
scope: Existing corporate pages (home, technology, experiences, delivery, services, about, contact, guides, shop, legal) treated as already published and preserved.
New corporate candidates such as professionals, installers and support recorded as planning candidates only.
Collision analysis against all 21 current route ids, the 7 admin ids and the 3 legacy redirect paths.
Per-candidate publication decision recorded as NOT_AUTHORIZED with the blocking gates named.
outOfScope: Any MAREA product, family, bundle or solution page (Phase 2 and Phase 3).
Any publication, route registration in src/, sitemap inclusion or indexation request.
Any claim wording that has not passed the claims policy.
entryCriteria: Phase 0 snapshot accepted.
D04-D06 bilingual IA, proposed route registry and slug/entity governance accepted.
D08/D09 canonical and indexation policies accepted, and D11 metadata contract available for the candidates.
exitCriteria: Every candidate has an entityId, ES and EN path, collision status, canonical/hreflang plan and a publication decision of NOT_AUTHORIZED.
No candidate is marked published, indexable or sitemapped; the route-gate matrix carries publicationAuthorized=false and indexationAuthorized=false for all of them.
Claims review outcome is recorded per candidate, including the finding references that remain open.
deliverables: Corporate IA candidate register with per-candidate publication decision
Collision report against current, admin and legacy surfaces
prohibitedActions: Treating a planning candidate as pre-authorised.
Creating a route, a page or a sitemap entry.
Publishing any MAREA reference inside a corporate candidate.
evidenceRequired: Candidate register with entityId and locale paths
Collision report with zero unresolved collisions
Claims review record per candidate

items.name: MAREA brand clearance prerequisite
items.objective: Establish that no MAREA page may become public before external brand, IP, claims and market-placement gates open, and define what a granted decision would have to contain. This phase cannot be completed by any agent and produces no page.
scope: Record the current state: TRADEMARK_LEGAL_CLEARANCE = NOT_GRANTED, MAREA_PUBLIC_USE = NO_GO (D-003 and D-059).
Define the minimum external decision set: counsel opinion on the class-9 conflict, written public-use decision, IP ownership chain, outbound licence decision.
Define what stays forbidden even after clearance: unverified certification, availability, price, safety and performance claims.
outOfScope: Filing, clearing, renaming or negotiating a trademark.
Creating, registering or publishing any MAREA URL.
Publishing MAREA in titles, descriptions, navigation, breadcrumbs or structured data.
entryCriteria: Phase 1 corporate candidates recorded (so MAREA work cannot hide inside a corporate page).
D-003 trademark gate and D-059 stricter public-brand rule accepted as binding.
MC-14 release gates register available with all 13 gates open.
exitCriteria: Either a written external clearance decision exists and is recorded with its scope, or the phase remains BLOCKED and no MAREA page may be created.
The forbidden-claim list is restated for the cleared scope, including certification, availability, price, ratings and performance.
No MAREA URL exists in any environment reachable by a crawler.
deliverables: Recorded clearance decision or a recorded BLOCKED verdict with the missing artefacts named
Restated forbidden-claim list for the cleared scope
prohibitedActions: Any public use of MAREA while public use is NO_GO, including og:image, social preview, footer attribution or JSON-LD brand.
Any agent-authored 'clearance' statement.
Any MAREA page, redirect or sitemap entry.
evidenceRequired: Written external clearance or public-use decision, or a BLOCKED record naming the missing artefacts
Gate status snapshot showing all blocking gates open

items.name: Product and solution page implementation (future milestones)
items.objective: Implement the product, family, bundle and solution pages in future implementation milestones, each with its own publication and structured-data authorisation. This is engineering work that is deliberately separate from SEO planning and is not started.
scope: One component per page, localised from LOCALIZED_ROUTES; no duplicated ES/EN implementation.
Per-page publication decision, per-page indexation decision and a structured-data decision that is independent of both.

Per-family gates: PILOT safety, AIS receive-only boundary, WATCH alert wording, WEATHER data licensing, FLEET tenancy, NAV navigational-aid boundary, DISPLAY/HUB conformity and compatibility evidence.
Quote-only and concept states expressed as content states, never as purchasable offers.
outOfScope: Any price, stock, availability or checkout for a MAREA product.
Any Product/Offer/AggregateRating/Review JSON-LD for MAREA.
Any SEO planning change (that is MC-15's closed scope).
entryCriteria: Phase 2 clearance for the scope being implemented.
D05 proposed route registry frozen for the page being built, with a collision-free ES/EN path pair.
D10 structured-data authorisation recorded per page type, and D11 metadata approved for both locales.
The relevant family gates open for the claims used on that page.
exitCriteria: Implementation reviewed and tested, with one component per page and locale parity verified.
Publication, indexation and structured data each recorded as independently authorised or explicitly withheld.
No page is released by this phase; release is Phase 5.
deliverables: Implemented pages behind an unpublished state
Per-page publication, indexation and structured-data authorisation records
prohibitedActions: Shipping a MAREA Product/Offer node, price, availability, rating or certification.
Creating a purchasable SKU from a hypothesis (D-007, D-009).
Publishing before Phase 5 authorisation.
evidenceRequired: Code review record and test output for each page
Locale parity and one-component verification
Structured-data authorisation record per page type

items.name: Controlled migration verification
items.objective: Verify, in a controlled non-public environment and against the Phase 0 snapshot, that redirects, canonical, hreflang, structured data and the sitemap behave exactly as decided, before any release decision.
scope: Redirect verification: the three EXISTING_ACTIVE legacy 301s still resolve in one hop to the same destinations; no new redirect exists; no PROPOSED_NOT_ACTIVE record has become active.

Canonical and hreflang verification: self-referencing absolute canonical on every indexable page, reciprocal groups, single x-default on the Spanish home, no invented EN alternate for an ES-only product.
Structured-data verification: valid JSON-LD, only whitelisted types, no MAREA Product/Offer, no price/availability/rating/certification claim.
Sitemap verification: set equality with the expected URL set, no private, admin, sample or blocked MAREA URL, alternates only when both locales are published.
Robots verification: no reliance on Disallow as a substitute for noindex; private and admin surfaces still noindex with the header.
outOfScope: Any change to live routing, headers, sitemap or robots while verifying.
Search Console submission or re-indexing requests.
Release, DNS or CDN changes.
entryCriteria: Phase 0 snapshot is authoritative and unchanged.
A candidate build artefact is identified by its git commit SHA and checksum (never by an invented deployment or release identifier).
A disposable database with the same fixture class used for the snapshot, so counts are comparable.
D07-D10 decisions frozen for the candidate under test.
exitCriteria: Verification report states, per URL family, that status, canonical, hreflang and robots are identical to the snapshot where preservation was decided, and identical to the plan where a change was authorised.
Redirect set equality: exactly the three inherited 301s active, zero chains, zero loops, zero cross-locale targets, zero destinations on a blocked page or a private page.
Sitemap set equality against the expected set, with every difference explained by dynamic data or content.
Zero blocked URL reachable as indexable, and zero structured-data restriction breach.
Any failed check blocks the phase; a failed phase cannot be reported as PASS.
deliverables: Migration verification report keyed to the Phase 0 snapshot
Redirect, canonical/hreflang, structured-data and sitemap check outputs
prohibitedActions: Verifying against a moving target or against production traffic.
Editing the snapshot to match the candidate.
Reporting an unexecuted or environment-blocked check as PASS.
evidenceRequired: Verification report with per-URL evidence
Candidate artefact SHA and checksum
Independent reviewer sign-off

items.name: Authorized release
items.objective: Release only with a separate written authorisation from the responsible human owner, after Phase 4 passes, with the rollback plan and its prerequisites verified. No agent may release, and MC-15 authorises nothing here.
scope: Record the authorisation: who authorised, what exactly is being released (URL set and code SHA), and what is explicitly not released.
Confirm the 13 gates that apply to the released scope, and record every gate that remains open together with its consequence.
Confirm the rollback prerequisites of D16 are true before release, not after an incident.
outOfScope: Any release performed by an autonomous agent.
Releasing a MAREA page before Phase 2 and Phase 3 are satisfied for that page.
Releasing a price, an offer or a stock state that has no approval.
entryCriteria: Phase 4 verification PASS with an independent reviewer.
A written authorisation naming the URL set, the code SHA and the excluded scope.
Rollback plan rehearsed at least once against the Phase 0 snapshot, with the checklist in D16 completed.
A named incident owner and an escalation channel available for the release window.
exitCriteria: Release executed by the authorised human owner and a change record created referencing the code SHA and the authorisation.
Post-release checks of Phase 6 started immediately, including redirect and canonical spot checks.
Any deviation from the authorised URL set is treated as an incident and triggers D16.
items.authorizationAuthority: COMMERCIAL_DIRECTOR with PROGRAMME_LEAD and an independent reviewer
deliverables: Change record with code SHA, URL set and excluded scope
Release-window incident owner and escalation channel
prohibitedActions: Releasing without a written authorisation.
Releasing a URL set larger than the one authorised.
Releasing before the rollback prerequisites are verified.
Any agent performing the release, merge or deployment.
evidenceRequired: Signed/recorded authorisation
Change record with SHA and URL set
Rollback rehearsal record

items.name: Post-release monitoring
items.objective: Monitor the released surface for crawl errors, redirect regressions, canonical/hreflang drift, sitemap coverage and indexation, and trigger the D16 rollback when a threshold is crossed. Monitoring access is a prerequisite, not an assumption.
scope: Scheduled verification of the redirect set (the three inherited 301s and any authorised new one) with one-hop and destination checks.
Sitemap fetch and diff against the expected URL set; report additions, removals and status changes.
Crawl-error and canonical/hreflang sampling across the preserved URL inventory.
Search Console coverage, impressions and indexation checks once access exists; until then the honest state is INDEXATION_UNVERIFIED.
Incident log with thresholds, decisions and evidence for every rollback trigger.
outOfScope: Changing content, routes, redirects or metadata to 'fix' a metric without authorisation.
Claiming indexation or ranking evidence that was not measured.
Any Marketing experiment that would invalidate the snapshot comparison.
entryCriteria: Phase 5 release executed with a change record.
Monitoring access established (Search Console or an equivalent first-party measurement); without it the phase runs in a reduced mode that must be declared.
The Phase 0 snapshot and the authorised expected URL set are available for diffing.
D16 thresholds and the named incident owner are agreed before the release window.
exitCriteria: An agreed stable window with no threshold breach, recorded with its measurement source.
Or a rollback executed and verified against the Phase 0 snapshot, with the incident closed and its cause recorded.
Every claim in the monitoring report traces to a measurement artefact; unmeasured metrics stay UNVERIFIED.
prohibitedActions: Inventing crawl, coverage or ranking numbers.
Declaring a stable window without measurements.
Silently reverting a change outside the D16 procedure.
evidenceRequired: Measurement artefacts (sitemap diff, redirect checks, coverage export when available)
Threshold breach log
Rollback record where applicable
